title: Punishing the Sicilian Pin Variation
author: Hanging Pawns

source.title: Sicilian Pin Variation (and why it's bad for black)

description: An interactive course built from Stjepan Tomić's video. Learn the one move that punishes 5...Bb4, and what to do against every Black reply.
permissionNote: Private demo built from this video to show its creator. Not published.

chapters.name: The Pin Variation and the move that punishes it

chapterData.name: The Pin Variation and the move that punishes it

children.comment: Hit g7 and ignore the pin. c3 isn't really hanging, because Qxg7 comes first. Every Black reply from here is uncomfortable.
Bd2 is playable, but Stjepan doesn't recommend it: after ...Nxc3 bxc3 Bf8 White's edge is small. Qg4 asks Black much harder questions.
The knight has to go to d5. The natural-looking ...Ne4 actually loses, and that's the next chapter. Now keep the initiative.
The refutation. It's forcing: the f6-knight is attacked and has to find a square.
Playable, but it's a cheap trick to answer a cheap trick: Black skips the pawn, plays ...d5 and is fine. Stjepan's move is more forcing.
It holds e4, but it's passive. Black plays ...d6 and gets a perfectly equal Scheveningen. Look for something more forcing.

moves.comment: The pin. Just like Bb5 in the Spanish, ...Bb4 pins the c3-knight so it no longer defends e4. Ignore it and Black simply takes the pawn. Several moves hold e4, but only one gives White a real edge. Find it.

chapterData.intro: We reach this after 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3. Black's ...Nf6 hits e4, and Nc3 is the main way to defend it. Now watch Black's next move: it's the Pin Variation, and you're about to learn the one move that punishes it.

chapterData.name: The ...Ne4 blunder

children.comment: The discovered check is blocked by a pawn that attacks the bishop, and the h8-rook is still hanging. Black loses material either way.
c3 is hanging twice, and it doesn't matter. g7 falls and the h8-rook is next.
Two attacks at once: the knight on e4 and the pawn on g7.

chapterData.intro: After 6.e5 you'd think it doesn't matter whether Black's knight goes to d5 or e4. It matters a lot. Watch Black play the natural ...Ne4.

chapterData.name: Castling walks into Bh6

children.comment: The rook stepped away, so go for the hook: h4-h5 undermines g6, and Black's king position collapses.
Also very strong. Stjepan goes straight for the hook on g6.
Also good. Stjepan goes straight for the hook on g6.
Don't take the rook. Defend c3 first. The rook on f8 isn't going anywhere, and ...g6 has given you a hook.
Also strong, and the engine rates it as highly as Nde2. Stjepan's move is Nde2, which simply secures c3.
Also good, and close to Nde2 by engine. Stjepan's move secures c3 first.
Also good by engine. Stjepan's move secures c3 first.
Grabbing the exchange is a mistake. Black's dark squares come alive after ...Qxf8. Defend c3 first.
Pile up on g7. Black has to answer with ...g6.

chapterData.intro: After 6...Nd5 7.Qg4, castling is the most common reply. It's also a disaster.

children.comment: The queen steps to a safe central square. Even against Black's best defence, White keeps a steady edge. Stjepan's summary: against the Pin Variation, remember e5 and Qg4.
Also fine. Stjepan's square is e4, right in the centre.
Also fine. Stjepan's square is e4, right in the centre.
Also fine. Stjepan's square is e4, right in the centre.
Unpin, so c3 is properly defended. Black's best reply is ...h5, kicking the queen. Without it Black is much worse.
Also good by engine. Stjepan's move is the simple unpin.
Also good by engine. Stjepan's move is the simple unpin.

moves.comment: The engine's choice: Black gives up castling to keep g7 covered without weakening the king. The bishop still pins the c3-knight. Deal with that.
